rules.legal_concept: Right of inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect public records in the custody of any officer; the statute grants the right to 'any person' without qualification as to who the requester is.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access).
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per contract. 'Any person' establishes standing regardless of identity.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency requirement to request public records; the right runs to 'any person,' not to residents or citizens of Arizona.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key. Arizona statute imposes no residency/citizenship limit; 'any person' is the operative term relied on. Absence of a residency clause captured affirmatively, not as a negative.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for non-commercial requests
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose to obtain public records, except that a requester must affirm the record is not for a commercial purpose and, if it is, must supply a commercial-purpose statement.
rules.trigger: Applies to non-commercial requests; commercial requests require a purpose statement (see AZ-0007, AZ-0008).
rules.source_language: At the time of the request, the requesting person shall affirm that the public record is not for a commercial purpose or, if the public record is for a commercial purpose, that the requesting person will provide a statement that explains the intended use pursuant to section 39-121.03, subsection A.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key, QUALIFIED: no general purpose statement is required, but a non-commercial affirmation is mandatory and a commercial statement is required for commercial use. Flag for reconciliation given the affirmation nuance.

rules.legal_concept: Access during office hours
rules.atomic_rule: Public records shall be open to inspection at all times during the office hours of the custodian's public body.
rules.trigger: Request to inspect during office hours.
rules.source_language: Public records and other matters in the custody of any officer shall be open to inspection by any person at all times during office hours.
rules.source_authority: Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 39-121; § 39-121.01(D)(1) ('during regular office hours')
rules.notes: Availability window is 'office hours' / 'regular office hours' — the city fills the specific hours; state sets no fixed number.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted request methods (in-person examination / mailed copy)
rules.atomic_rule: A person may request to examine or be furnished copies in person during regular office hours, or may request that the custodian mail a copy of a public record to the requester.
rules.trigger: A request is made.
rules.source_language: Any person may request to examine or be furnished copies, printouts or photographs of any public record during regular office hours or may request that the custodian mail a copy of any public record not otherwise available on the public body's website to the requesting person.
rules.notes: No prescribed request form or writing requirement in statute; oral and written both implied.

rules.legal_concept: Mailed-copy right limited to records not on the public body's website
rules.atomic_rule: The right to demand a mailed copy applies only to a public record not otherwise available on the public body's website.
rules.trigger: Requester asks custodian to mail a copy and the record is available on the public body's website.
rules.source_language: Any person may request to examine or be furnished copies, printouts or photographs of any public record during regular office hours or may request that the custodian mail a copy of any public record not otherwise available on the public body's website to the requesting person.
rules.notes: Modifies the mail-request permission in AZ-0005; does not limit in-person inspection.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial-purpose affirmation at time of request
rules.atomic_rule: At the time of the request the requester shall affirm the record is not for a commercial purpose, or, if it is, agree to provide a commercial-purpose statement under § 39-121.03(A).
rules.trigger: A request is made (every request).
rules.source_language: At the time of the request, the requesting person shall affirm that the public record is not for a commercial purpose or, if the public record is for a commercial purpose, that the requesting person will provide a statement that explains the intended use pursuant to section 39-121.03, subsection A.
rules.notes: Intake gate that routes the request onto the commercial fee track (AZ-0019) when applicable.

rules.legal_concept: Statement of commercial purpose
rules.atomic_rule: A requester seeking copies for a commercial purpose shall provide a statement setting forth the commercial purpose for which the copies will be used.
rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose (as defined in § 39-121.03(D)).
rules.source_language: When a person requests copies, printouts or photographs of public records for a commercial purpose, the person shall provide a statement setting forth the commercial purpose for which the copies, printouts or photographs will be used.
rules.notes: Precondition to furnishing records for commercial use and to the commercial fee calculation.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'commercial purpose'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Commercial purpose' means use of a public record for sale or resale, for producing a document containing the record for sale, obtaining names/addresses for solicitation, or any purpose from which the purchaser can reasonably anticipate monetary gain; it excludes use as evidence or research for evidence in a judicial or quasi-judicial action.
rules.trigger: Classification of a request as commercial vs. non-commercial.
rules.source_language: For the purposes of this section, "commercial purpose" means the use of a public record for the purpose of sale or resale or for the purpose of producing a document containing all or part of the copy, printout or photograph for sale or the obtaining of names and addresses from public records for the purpose of solicitation or the sale of names and addresses to another for the purpose of solicitation or for any purpose in which the purchaser can reasonably anticipate the receipt of monetary gain from the direct or indirect use of the public record. Commercial purpose does not mean the use of a public record as evidence or as research for evidence in an action in any judicial or quasi-judicial body.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: a definition the software branches on (drives fee basis and routing).

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'public body' (coverage of municipalities)
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public body' includes the state, any county, city, town, school district, political subdivision or tax-supported district, and their branches/departments/boards, plus any public organization supported in whole or part by public monies — establishing which entities are subject to the request process.
rules.trigger: Determining whether the responding entity is covered.
rules.source_language: "Public body" means this state, any county, city, town, school district, political subdivision or tax-supported district in this state, any branch, department, board, bureau, commission, council or committee of the foregoing, and any public organization or agency, supported in whole or in part by monies from this state or any political subdivision of this state, or expending monies provided by this state or any political subdivision of this state.
rules.notes: Keeper: coverage definition the platform branches on to determine applicability to a municipal body. Officer definition in (A)(1) excluded as non-operational for request handling.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to promptly furnish records
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall promptly furnish the requested copies, printouts or photographs (a soft-standard timing duty, not a numeric deadline).
rules.trigger: A valid request for copies is received.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
rules.notes: Soft deadline per contract: config_home=structural, no invented day-count. Arizona courts (e.g., West Valley View v. Maricopa County Sheriff's Office, 216 Ariz. 225 (App. 2007)) gloss 'promptly' as production with reasonable promptness; not automated here.

rules.legal_concept: Access deemed denied for failure to promptly respond or provide withholding index
rules.atomic_rule: Access is deemed denied if the custodian fails to promptly respond to a request or fails to provide the requester an index of records withheld under § 39-121.01(D)(2).
rules.trigger: Custodian's failure to promptly respond, or failure to provide the required withholding index.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: constructive denial arises upon failure to 'promptly respond' from request receipt
rules.source_language: Access to a public record is deemed denied if a custodian fails to promptly respond to a request for production of a public record or fails to provide to the requesting person an index of any record or categories of records that are withheld from production pursuant to subsection D, paragraph 2 of this section.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: deemed/constructive denial trigger. Terminal event that moves the request to a denied state and opens the judicial appeal path (AZ-0025). Remedy amounts intentionally excluded.

rules.legal_concept: Access to make own copies when custodian lacks facilities
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian lacks facilities to make copies of a record the person has a right to inspect, the person shall be granted access to make copies, while the record stays in the custodian's possession and under the custodian's supervision.
rules.trigger: Custodian does not have copying/printout/photograph facilities.
rules.source_language: If the custodian of a public record does not have facilities for making copies, printouts or photographs of a public record that a person has a right to inspect, the person shall be granted access to the public record for the purpose of making copies, printouts or photographs. The copies, printouts or photographs shall be made while the public record is in the possession, custody and control of the custodian of the public record and shall be subject to the supervision of the custodian.
rules.notes: Production-method branch.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic records and embedded metadata are public records subject to disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: When a public record is maintained in an electronic medium, it must be produced in that electronic medium including embedded metadata, on request.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks an electronically-maintained record and/or its metadata.
rules.source_language: We hold that when a public entity maintains a public record in an electronic format, the electronic version, including any embedded metadata, is subject to disclosure under our public records laws.
rules.source_authority: Lake v. City of Phoenix, 222 Ariz. 547, 218 P.3d 1004 (2009)
rules.notes: Judicially Established operational rule on electronic format/metadata not stated in statute. is_paraphrase=true: full opinion text not opened this pass; quotation approximates the holding — flag for verbatim verification against the official Arizona Supreme Court opinion.

rules.legal_concept: Index of withheld records and reasons
rules.atomic_rule: If requested, the custodian of an agency's records shall furnish an index of records or categories of records withheld and the reasons for withholding.
rules.trigger: Requester asks for an index and records have been withheld; applies to an 'agency' custodian.
rules.source_language: If requested, the custodian of the records of an agency shall also furnish an index of records or categories of records that have been withheld and the reasons the records or categories of records have been withheld from the requesting person.
rules.notes: Failure to provide this index is itself a constructive-denial trigger (AZ-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Privileged/confidential information excluded from withholding index
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall not include in the withholding index information that is expressly made privileged or confidential by statute or court order.
rules.trigger: Preparation of the withholding index (AZ-0015).
rules.source_language: The custodian shall not include in the index information that is expressly made privileged or confidential in statute or a court order.
rules.notes: Constrains the content of the index produced under AZ-0015.

rules.legal_concept: Agencies excluded from the index obligation
rules.atomic_rule: The withholding-index duty applies to an 'agency' as defined in § 41-1001 but excludes the Department of Public Safety, the ADOT Motor Vehicle Division, the Department of Juvenile Corrections, and the State Department of Corrections; and non-agency public bodies cannot be compelled to furnish an index under this paragraph.
rules.trigger: Custodian is one of the excluded departments or a non-agency public body.
rules.source_language: This paragraph shall not be construed by an administrative tribunal or a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent or require an order compelling a public body other than an agency to furnish an index. For the purposes of this paragraph, "agency" has the same meaning prescribed in section 41-1001 but does not include the department of public safety, the department of transportation motor vehicle division, the department of juvenile corrections and the state department of corrections.
rules.notes: Scope exception to the index requirement; mostly state-agency-specific but limits which municipal/agency custodians the index duty binds.

rules.legal_concept: Permission to charge a fee for copies (non-commercial)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may charge a fee for furnishing copies, printouts or photographs if the facilities are available; the statute sets no rate.
rules.trigger: Copies are furnished and copying facilities are available.
rules.source_language: The custodian of such records shall promptly furnish such copies, printouts or photographs and may charge a fee if the facilities are available, except that public records for purposes listed in section 39-122 or 39-127 shall be furnished without charge.
rules.notes: constraint_basis=soft-standard: state authorizes a fee but supplies no number; the city sets the per-copy rate. Arizona case law limits non-commercial fees to copying-related costs (not personnel time); that gloss is not automated here.

rules.legal_concept: Fee components for commercial-purpose reproductions
rules.atomic_rule: For a commercial-purpose request the charge may include (1) a portion of the cost to the public body for obtaining the original or copies, (2) a reasonable fee for time, materials, equipment and personnel in producing the reproduction, and (3) the value of the reproduction on the commercial market as best determined by the public body.
rules.trigger: Request classified as commercial purpose and commercial-purpose statement provided.
rules.source_language: Upon being furnished the statement the custodian of such records may furnish reproductions, the charge for which shall include the following: 1. A portion of the cost to the public body for obtaining the original or copies of the documents, printouts or photographs. 2. A reasonable fee for the cost of time, materials, equipment and personnel in producing such reproduction. 3. The value of the reproduction on the commercial market as best determined by the public body.
rules.notes: Same fee concept family as AZ-0018 but a distinct commercial basis; state defines the components, the city determines the amounts (hence soft-standard, includes a 'reasonable fee' and market-value element).

rules.legal_concept: No charge for records used in claims against the United States
rules.atomic_rule: State, county, and municipal officers shall furnish, without charge, searches for and certified copies of public records needed in support of a claim or benefit application against the United States.
rules.trigger: Records requested for use in a claim/benefit application against the United States by a claimant, guardian, or attorney.
rules.source_language: Free searches for and copies of public records to be used in claims against United States; liability for noncompliance. [Officers] shall furnish without charge certified copies of and make searches for public records to be used in prosecuting any claim or securing any benefit to which the claimant may be entitled from the United States.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: the fetched source returned a summary with only fragment quotes; the reconstructed clause needs verbatim confirmation against azleg. Fee-waiver branch cross-referenced by AZ-0011/AZ-0018.

rules.legal_concept: Free copy of police report for crime victims
rules.atomic_rule: A victim of a listed offense (or the victim's attorney, or immediate family of a deceased/incapacitated victim) has the right to receive one copy of the police report, and audio/video recordings, at no charge.
rules.trigger: Requester is a qualifying crime victim (or representative) requesting the police report of that offense.
rules.source_language: Free copies of police reports, audio recordings, video recordings and transcripts for crime victims. [The victim] has the right to receive one copy of the police report... at no cost.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: source returned a summary with fragment quotes; needs verbatim confirmation. Distinct fee-waiver + qualification workflow (requester must qualify as victim).

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment for copying and postage on mailed copies
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require a person requesting a mailed copy to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges.
rules.trigger: Requester asks the custodian to mail a copy.
rules.source_language: The custodian may require any person requesting that the custodian mail a copy of any public record to pay in advance for any copying and postage charges.
rules.notes: constraint_basis=ceiling: advance charge is limited to copying + postage; the city supplies the actual amounts. Applies only to mailed copies.

rules.legal_concept: Commercial reproductions provided upon payment of the determined fee
rules.atomic_rule: If no gubernatorial order issues within thirty days of a custodian's application, the custodian shall provide the commercial reproductions upon being paid the fee determined under § 39-121.03(A).
rules.trigger: Governor issues no prohibiting order within 30 days of the custodian's application.
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from custodian's application to the governor
rules.source_language: If no order is issued within thirty days of the date of application, the custodian of public records shall provide such copies, printouts or photographs upon being paid the fee determined pursuant to subsection A.
rules.notes: Release is conditioned on payment of the AZ-0019 fee once the 30-day governor window lapses without an order.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian petition to the governor to bar a commercial purpose
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian determines a stated commercial purpose is a misuse or abuse, the custodian may apply to the governor; the governor shall determine misuse/abuse and, if so, issue an executive order prohibiting furnishing records for that commercial purpose.
rules.trigger: Custodian believes the stated commercial purpose is a misuse or abuse of public records.
rules.clock_spec: governor may act within 30 calendar-days of the custodian's application (no order in 30 days = records must be furnished)
rules.source_language: If the custodian of a public record determines that the commercial purpose stated in the statement is a misuse of public records or is an abuse of the right to receive public records, the custodian may apply to the governor requesting that the governor by executive order prohibit the furnishing of copies, printouts or photographs for such commercial purpose. The governor, upon application from a custodian of public records, shall determine whether the commercial purpose is a misuse or an abuse of the public record. If the governor determines that the public record shall not be provided for such commercial purpose the governor shall issue an executive order prohibiting the providing of such public records for such commercial purpose.
rules.notes: Arizona-specific structural review path (custodian-initiated, decided by the governor). Its 30-day lapse feeds the terminal release rule AZ-0023.

rules.legal_concept: Special action in superior court to challenge denial
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access to or the right to copy public records may appeal the denial through a special action in the superior court against the officer or public body.
rules.trigger: Denial (actual or constructive) of access or copying.
rules.source_language: Any person who has requested to examine or copy public records pursuant to this article and who has been denied access to or the right to copy such records may appeal the denial through a special action in the superior court pursuant to the rules of procedure for special actions against the officer or public body.
rules.notes: Judicial appeal path (namespaced appeal.judicial). Arizona provides no internal administrative appeal stage before court; review goes directly to superior court via special action.

rules.legal_concept: Victim's special action within a criminal case
rules.atomic_rule: A victim denied access to a public record in the course of a criminal case in superior court may appeal the denial through a special action within the criminal case.
rules.trigger: Victim denied access to a public record during a superior-court criminal case.
rules.source_language: If a victim is denied access to a public record pursuant to this article in the course of a criminal case in superior court, the victim may appeal the denial through a special action within the criminal case.
rules.notes: Distinct judicial route for victims; runs inside the criminal case rather than as a stand-alone special action.

rules.legal_concept: Priority processing of crime-victim police-report requests
rules.atomic_rule: A law enforcement agency shall prioritize the processing and providing of each police report requested by a crime victim under § 39-127.
rules.trigger: A crime-victim request for a police report under § 39-127 is received.
rules.source_language: The law enforcement agency shall prioritize the processing and providing of each police report [requested under this section].
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: fetched source gave a summary with a fragment quote; needs verbatim confirmation. Alters processing order/priority, so passes the inclusion test.

structural_branches.description: AZ-0011: the response duty is a soft 'promptly' standard, not a numeric deadline — the engine applies a standard rather than counting days.
AZ-0012: failure to promptly respond OR to provide the withholding index is a terminal event that moves the request to a denied state and opens judicial review.
AZ-0024: Arizona-specific custodian-initiated review path decided by the Governor, with a 30-day window whose lapse forces release (AZ-0023).
AZ-0025: review of a denial runs directly to superior court via special action — no internal administrative appeal stage precedes it.
AZ-0026: a separate judicial branch for victims, litigated inside the pending criminal case.
AZ-0014: electronic records must be produced in native electronic form including embedded metadata (judicially established).
AZ-0015: on request, an agency custodian must produce a Vaughn-style index of withheld records and reasons; its omission is itself a denial trigger.
AZ-0027: crime-victim police-report requests are processed on a priority track.
AZ-0013: when the custodian lacks copying facilities, the requester is granted supervised access to make copies on site.

material_negatives.note: No statutory duty to acknowledge a request within a fixed period. Arizona sets no numeric acknowledgment deadline; the only timing standard is 'promptly furnish' (AZ-0011) and constructive denial on failure to promptly respond (AZ-0012). Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.
No numeric statutory response/production deadline (no 'X business days'). The standard is the soft 'promptly' term. Captured as a soft-standard rule, not a value.
No explicit statutory clarification clock, duty to assist the requester in narrowing an unclear or overbroad request, or non-response/abandonment trigger found in Title 39, Chapter 1.
No statutory requirement that a municipality assign a tracking number or maintain a request log/register for public-records requests found.

No general statutory segregate-and-release / redaction-of-exempt-portions procedure stated in the core access statutes; withholding is instead documented via the § 39-121.01(D)(2) index (AZ-0015). Segregability obligations, if any, arise from specific exemption statutes and case law not inventoried this pass.

No internal/administrative appeal stage for a denied requester before court; review is directly to superior court by special action (AZ-0025). Emitted affirmatively as the absence of an administrative appeal branch, relevant to cross-state comparison of appeal paths.
No general statutory advance-deposit/estimate regime for large non-commercial requests; the only advance-payment authority found is for copying + postage on mailed copies (AZ-0022).
No statewide statutory per-page copy rate for ordinary (non-commercial) requests; the statute grants only permission to charge a fee (AZ-0018), leaving the value to the municipality.

rules.legal_concept: Public records open to inspection by any person
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect any public record at reasonable times, except as otherwise provided in the Act or by law; no requester qualification is imposed.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right of access)
rules.source_language: All public records shall be open for inspection by any person at reasonable times, except as provided in this part 2 or as otherwise provided by law.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per the universal-access-symmetry instruction. 'Any person' is the eligibility gate; no residency, purpose, or status qualification appears in the operative clause.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request public records
rules.atomic_rule: CORA imposes no residency or citizenship requirement; the right to inspect runs to 'any person' without geographic qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The Act extends inspection to 'any person' and states no residency, citizenship, or geographic qualification; the absence of any residency condition is derived from the 'any person' grant in 24-72-203(1)(a).
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared canonical key per universal-access-symmetry rule (never as a material negative). Paraphrase: statute states the absence implicitly via 'any person', not by an express no-residency clause.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required for general public records
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose or reason to inspect general public records; the right runs to any person at reasonable times.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The general inspection right in 24-72-203(1)(a) is unconditional as to purpose; no statement-of-purpose is required for ordinary public records (derived from the unqualified 'any person ... at reasonable times' grant).
rules.notes: Shared canonical key per universal-access-symmetry. Caveat for later pass: certain special record categories (e.g., records of names/addresses used for solicitation under 24-72-204/205.5) do carry a purpose/use restriction; this rule covers only ordinary records.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'custodian'
rules.atomic_rule: The 'custodian' is the official custodian or any authorized person having personal custody and control of the public records in question; this identifies who must respond and drives routing.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: "Custodian" means and includes the official custodian or any authorized person having personal custody and control of the public records in question.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #1: definition the software branches on for routing / who-must-respond.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may adopt rules for protection of records
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may make and enforce rules reasonably necessary for the protection of the records and to prevent unnecessary interference with the discharge of duties.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The official custodian of any public records may make such rules with reference to the inspection of such records as are reasonably necessary for the protection of such records and the prevention of unnecessary interference with the regular discharge of the duties of the custodian or the custodian's office.
rules.notes: Source of local intake/procedure rules (e.g., request form, hours). Explains why intake format is a municipal parameter rather than a statewide fixed rule.

rules.legal_concept: Notice when records not in custodian's custody
rules.atomic_rule: If the requested records are not in the custody or control of the person to whom application is made, that person shall so notify the applicant in writing and, if known, state which custodian has custody or control.
rules.trigger: Applied-to person lacks custody/control of the requested record
rules.source_language: If the public records requested are not in the custody or control of the person to whom application is made, such person shall forthwith notify the applicant of this fact, in writing if requested by the applicant. In such notification, such person shall state, in detail to the best of such person's knowledge and belief, the reason for the absence of the records from such person's custody or control, their location, and what person then has custody or control of the records.
rules.notes: Routing/wrong-department rule (keeper-sliver #1 family). 'forthwith' notice is a soft-timed communication; primary effect is routing to the correct custodian.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable time for inspection presumed three working days
rules.atomic_rule: When records are not readily available, the custodian must set a date and hour for inspection within a reasonable time after the request; a reasonable time is presumed to be three working days or less.
rules.trigger: Requested records are not readily available at time of request
rules.clock_spec: presumptive ceiling: 3 working days from request receipt (rebuttable presumption of 'reasonable time')
rules.source_language: The date and hour set for the inspection of records not readily available at the time of the request shall be within a reasonable time after the request. As used in this subsection (3), a "reasonable time" shall be presumed to be three working days or less.
rules.notes: Core response clock. Number is a rebuttable presumption (a ceiling on 'reasonable'), not an absolute fixed deadline — hence constraint_basis=ceiling with the soft-presumption noted.

rules.legal_concept: Extension for extenuating circumstances (max seven working days)
rules.atomic_rule: The three-working-day period may be extended when extenuating circumstances exist, but the extension shall not exceed seven working days.
rules.trigger: Extenuating circumstances exist (as defined in 24-72-203(3)(b))
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 7 additional working days beyond the presumptive 3-working-day period
rules.source_language: Such period may be extended if extenuating circumstances exist. However, such period of extension shall not exceed seven working days.
rules.notes: Extension caps total at 3 + 7 working days. constraint_basis=ceiling (shall not exceed).

rules.legal_concept: Written finding of extenuating circumstances within three-day period
rules.atomic_rule: A finding that extenuating circumstances exist must be made in writing by the custodian and provided to the requester within the three-working-day period.
rules.trigger: Custodian invokes an extenuating-circumstances extension
rules.clock_spec: written finding due within 3 working days of the request (before extension takes effect)
rules.source_language: A finding that extenuating circumstances exist shall be made in writing by the custodian and shall be provided to the person making the request within the three-day period.
rules.notes: Required notice/document gating the extension; a structural step the engine must execute within the base window.

rules.legal_concept: Extenuating circumstances barred for a single identified document
rules.atomic_rule: Extenuating circumstances can never apply to a request that relates to a single, specifically identified document.
rules.trigger: Request relates to a single, specifically identified document
rules.source_language: In no event can extenuating circumstances apply to a request that relates to a single, specifically identified document.
rules.notes: Blocks the extension branch for single-document requests; keeps the base 3-working-day ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of extenuating circumstances
rules.atomic_rule: Extenuating circumstances are limited to enumerated situations, including a broadly stated request encompassing all or substantially all of a large category of records without sufficient specificity to allow preparation within the three-day period.
rules.trigger: Custodian evaluates whether an extension is available
rules.source_language: Extenuating circumstances shall apply only when ... [t]he request for records is for a broadly stated request that encompasses all or substantially all of a large category of records and the request is without sufficient specificity to allow the custodian reasonably to prepare or gather the records within the three-day period; [and other enumerated situations including requests requiring gathering of a large volume of records that would interfere with the custodian's other public-service duties, and, for the general assembly, when it is in session].
rules.notes: Bracketed portions summarize the remaining enumerated items (large-volume interference; general-assembly-in-session) captured from the opened source; the broadly-stated-request clause is verbatim. Full enumeration should be re-verified against the codified subsection in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Production in sortable/searchable digital format
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record is stored in a digital format that is sortable, the custodian shall provide a copy in a sortable format; if stored in a searchable format, in a searchable format.
rules.trigger: Requested record is maintained in a digital sortable or searchable format
rules.source_language: If a public record is stored in a digital format that is sortable, the custodian shall provide a copy of the public record in a sortable format. [Companion provision: if stored in a searchable format, the custodian shall provide it in a searchable format.]
rules.notes: Tiered native-format production duty. The sortable-format sentence is verbatim; the searchable-tier companion is captured from the opened source and should be re-verified verbatim in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Exception to native-format production (feasibility / licensing)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian need not produce in the sortable/searchable format if doing so would violate a copyright or licensing agreement, or if it is not technologically or practically feasible to remove withholdable information or to provide the format without purchasing new software.
rules.trigger: Copyright/licensing conflict, or technological/practical infeasibility to produce the native format or redact
rules.source_language: [The custodian is not required to produce a record in a sortable or searchable format if doing so would violate a copyright or licensing agreement, or if it is not technologically or practically feasible to remove information that may be withheld or to provide the record in the requested format without the purchase of software.]
rules.notes: Paraphrase of the (3.5) exceptions as captured from the opened source; exact statutory wording of the feasibility/licensing exceptions should be verified verbatim in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Written statement of grounds for denial
rules.atomic_rule: On denial of access, if the applicant requests it, the custodian must furnish forthwith a written statement of the grounds for denial citing the law or regulation under which access is denied.
rules.trigger: Custodian denies access and the applicant requests a written statement
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "forthwith" from the applicant's request for a written statement
rules.source_language: If the custodian denies access to any public record, the applicant may request a written statement of the grounds for the denial, which statement shall cite the law or regulation under which access is denied and shall be furnished forthwith to the applicant.
rules.notes: Soft deadline ('forthwith') -> config_home structural per soft-standard rule. This written statement is a prerequisite document for the judicial show-cause path.

rules.legal_concept: Segregability / inspection of non-withheld portions
rules.atomic_rule: Where only portions of a record are withholdable (e.g., specialized details of security arrangements or investigations), the custodian may deny inspection of only those portions and shall allow inspection of the remaining portions.
rules.trigger: A record contains both withholdable and disclosable portions
rules.source_language: A custodian may deny the right of inspection of only those portions of a record ... that contain specialized details of security arrangements or investigations and shall allow inspection of the remaining portions.
rules.notes: Segregability duty captured verbatim from the security-arrangements exemption; it expresses the redact-and-release principle. Whether a broader general segregability clause exists elsewhere in 204 should be confirmed in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee per standard page
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a copy on a standard page
rules.source_language: A custodian may charge a fee not to exceed twenty-five cents per standard page for a copy of a public record or a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page.
rules.notes: State sets a ceiling ($0.25/standard page); the municipality supplies the operative value at or below it. constraint_basis=ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost fee for non-standard-page copies
rules.atomic_rule: For a copy, printout, or photograph in a format other than a standard page, the custodian may charge a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing it.
rules.trigger: Copy provided in a format other than a standard page
rules.source_language: ... a fee not to exceed the actual cost of providing a copy, printout, or photograph of a public record in a format other than a standard page.
rules.notes: Actual-cost ceiling for non-standard formats; municipality supplies the operative charge under the cap.

rules.legal_concept: Research-and-retrieval hourly fee cap
rules.atomic_rule: After the first hour, the custodian may charge a fee for research and retrieval of public records not to exceed thirty dollars per hour.
rules.trigger: Research and retrieval time exceeds the first free hour
rules.source_language: After the first hour of time has been expended, the custodian may charge a fee for the research and retrieval of public records that shall not exceed thirty dollars per hour.
rules.notes: The $30/hour statutory ceiling is periodically adjusted for inflation by the Director of Research of the Legislative Council (the current CPI-adjusted maximum is higher than $30 and should be pulled from the current published figure). constraint_basis=ceiling; municipality sets its own rate at or below the current maximum.

rules.legal_concept: First hour of research and retrieval free
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall not impose any charge for the first hour of time expended in research and retrieval of public records.
rules.trigger: Research and retrieval performed on a request
rules.source_language: Under any such policy, the custodian shall not impose a charge for the first hour of time expended in connection with the research and retrieval of public records.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory free allowance (1 hour). Not municipally variable — constraint_basis=fixed.

rules.legal_concept: Published fee policy prerequisite to charging research/retrieval fees
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may impose a research-and-retrieval fee only if, before receiving the request, it has posted on its website or otherwise published a written policy specifying the applicable conditions and the amount of any current fee.
rules.trigger: Custodian intends to charge a research-and-retrieval fee
rules.source_language: A custodian may impose a fee in response to a request for the research and retrieval of public records only if the custodian has, prior to the date of receiving the request, either posted on the custodian's website or otherwise published a written policy that specifies the applicable conditions concerning the research and retrieval of public records by the custodian, including the amount of any current fee.
rules.notes: Gating precondition: no published policy => no research/retrieval fee may be charged. Structural prerequisite the engine must check before applying the fee parameter.

rules.legal_concept: No transmission fee for records sent by email
rules.atomic_rule: No transmission fee may be charged to the requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail.
rules.trigger: Records are transmitted to the requester via electronic mail
rules.source_language: No transmission fees may be charged to the record requester for transmitting public records via electronic mail.
rules.notes: Fixed $0 for email transmission. Modeled as a parameter fixed at zero (rule_type Prohibition). Subsection number (1)(b) captured from opened source; verify exact placement in later pass.

rules.legal_concept: District court application for order to show cause
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied the right to inspect a record, or who alleges a violation of 24-72-203(3.5), may apply to the district court where the record is found for an order directing the custodian to show cause why inspection should not be permitted.
rules.trigger: Denial of inspection, or alleged violation of the digital-format provision
rules.source_language: Any person denied the right to inspect any record covered by this part 2 or who alleges a violation of section 24-72-203 (3.5) may apply to the district court of the district wherein the record is found for an order directing the custodian of such record to show cause why the custodian should not permit the inspection of such record.
rules.notes: Judicial-review path (namespaced appeal.judicial.*). CORA has no internal administrative appeal stage; enforcement is judicial only.

rules.legal_concept: Fourteen-day pre-filing written notice to custodian
rules.atomic_rule: At least fourteen days before filing an application with the district court, the person denied inspection must file a written notice with the custodian.
rules.trigger: Requester intends to file a district court show-cause application
rules.clock_spec: 14 days: written notice to custodian must precede filing by at least 14 days
rules.source_language: ... except that, at least fourteen days prior to filing an application with the district court, the person who has been denied the right to inspect the record shall file a written notice with the custodian ...
rules.notes: Mandatory pre-suit notice window; a required step preceding the judicial path. This 14-day period is intended for the parties to confer/resolve before litigation.

rules.legal_concept: Expedited pre-filing notice (three business days)
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester states an expedited need in the required written notice, the notice (including a factual basis for the expedited need) must be provided to the custodian at least three business days before filing the application.
rules.trigger: Requester asserts an expedited need for the record
rules.clock_spec: 3 business days: expedited written notice (with factual basis) must precede filing by at least 3 business days
rules.source_language: If the person who has been denied access to inspect a record states in the required written notice to the custodian that the person needs to pursue access to the record on an expedited basis, the person must provide such written notice, including a factual basis of the expedited need for the record, to the custodian at least three business days prior to the date on which the person files the application with the district court.
rules.notes: Shortens the pre-suit notice from 14 days to 3 business days when an expedited need with factual basis is asserted.

rules.legal_concept: Show-cause hearing held at earliest practical time
rules.atomic_rule: The hearing on a show-cause application must be held at the earliest practical time.
rules.trigger: A show-cause application is filed
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest practical time" from filing of the application
rules.source_language: Hearing on the application described in subsection (5)(a) of this section must be held at the earliest practical time.
rules.notes: Soft deadline -> config_home structural per soft-standard rule; no numeric day-count invented.

material_negatives.note: CORA sets a response/inspection window (presumptive 3 working days, 24-72-203(3)(b)) but prescribes no separate mandatory acknowledgment-of-receipt deadline distinct from providing access. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No express statutory 'deemed denial' or constructive-denial clock (silence for N days = denial). CORA's remedy trigger is an affirmative denial of access (24-72-204(4)-(5)); it does not convert non-response into an automatic denial after a fixed period. Keeper-sliver #3 therefore yields a negative for Colorado.

No statute mandates that a request be in writing or on a specific form. The custodian may adopt reasonable rules (24-72-203(2)(a)); intake format is thus a municipal-level rule, not a statewide fixed requirement.

The statute authorizes copy and research/retrieval fees but states no statutory deposit/prepayment cap or mandatory prepayment procedure. Custodian prepayment practices are local and not fixed by statute in the sections reviewed.

No separate statutory clarification-and-toll mechanism for vague requests. A broadly stated/insufficiently specific request instead qualifies as an 'extenuating circumstance' extending the response period (24-72-203(3)(b)); there is no distinct clarification clock that tolls or resets the deadline.

The sections reviewed do not establish a general commercial-purpose fee surcharge for ordinary records. (Special provisions for records of names/addresses used for solicitation exist under 24-72-204/205.5 and belong to a later special-records pass.)

structural_branches.description: Extenuating-circumstances extension path: on qualifying triggers the engine adds up to 7 working days, but only after issuing a written finding within the base 3-working-day window (CO-0009) and only if the request is not for a single identified document (CO-0010).
Tiered digital-format production branch: sortable-stored records produced sortable, searchable-stored records produced searchable (CO-0012), with a feasibility/licensing off-ramp (CO-0013).
On denial, a requester-triggered branch producing a written, law-citing statement of grounds 'forthwith' (CO-0014), which also serves as the predicate document for the judicial path.
Fee-eligibility gate: research/retrieval fees may be charged only after a pre-published written fee policy exists; without it the fee branch is unavailable (CO-0020).

Judicial-only enforcement path (no internal administrative appeal): mandatory 14-day pre-suit notice to custodian (CO-0023), a 3-business-day expedited variant (CO-0024), then a district-court show-cause hearing at the earliest practical time (CO-0025).

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person may inspect, examine, and obtain copies of public records held by a custodian; access is not limited to a class of requesters.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person, and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per symmetry rule. 'By any person' is the operative eligibility grant.

rules.legal_concept: No disclosure of purpose or motive required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may not be required to disclose the purpose or motive for inspecting, examining, or copying public records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional)
rules.source_language: No person requesting to inspect and examine public records, or to obtain copies thereof, shall be required to disclose the purpose or motive for the request.
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared key, never a negative.

rules.legal_concept: No residency requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency requirement to request public records; access runs to any person.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person...
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry. NC imposes no residency limit; the no-residency conclusion is inferred from the 'any person' grant (statute does not use the word 'residency'). Source Language is the verbatim any-person clause.

rules.legal_concept: Inspection at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must permit inspection and examination at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision.
rules.trigger: Request to inspect/examine
rules.source_language: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person...
rules.notes: 'Reasonable times' and 'reasonable supervision' are undefined standards; not converted to a number.

rules.legal_concept: Copies furnished 'as promptly as possible'
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian must furnish copies as promptly as possible upon payment of any lawful fees.
rules.trigger: Request for copies received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" from request receipt
rules.source_language: ...and shall, as promptly as possible, furnish copies thereof upon payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Soft deadline; Config Home structural per contract. NC sets no fixed numeric response/acknowledgment deadline (see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Online availability satisfies copy duty
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy the access/copy duty by making records available online in a viewable, printable/savable format; if so maintained, it need not provide copies any other way.
rules.trigger: Agency maintains the record online in a viewable/printable/savable format
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian may satisfy the requirements in subsection (a) of this section by making public records available online in a format that allows a person to view the public record and print or save the public record to obtain a copy. If the public agency or custodian maintains public records online in a format that allows a person to view and print or save the public records to obtain a copy, the public agency or custodian is not required to provide copies to these public records in any other way.
rules.notes: A processing branch: online-availability path can terminate the copy-production obligation.

rules.legal_concept: Policy: copies free or at minimal cost; 'minimal cost' defined
rules.atomic_rule: State policy is that people obtain copies free or at minimal cost, where 'minimal cost' means the actual cost of reproducing the record.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: Therefore, it is the policy of this State that the people may obtain copies of their public records and public information free or at minimal cost unless otherwise specifically provided by law. As used herein, "minimal cost" shall mean the actual cost of reproducing the public record or public information.
rules.notes: General fee-policy definition that grounds the operative actual-cost ceiling in § 132-6.2(b). Definition the software branches on for fee basis.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivision may not use NDA to restrict access
rules.atomic_rule: A political subdivision may not withhold or deny access on the basis of a nondisclosure agreement entered to restrict access to records subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: Agency asserts an NDA as basis to restrict access
rules.source_language: No political subdivision of this State may enter into a nondisclosure agreement in order to restrict access to public records subject to disclosure under this Chapter. The contract by which a political subdivision of this State agrees not to disclose information deemed confidential under State law shall be a public record, unless the existence of the contract is also deemed confidential under State law.
rules.notes: Gates a denial basis: an NDA cannot be the ground for withholding disclosable records. Added by 2023-134/2023-138.

rules.legal_concept: No denial because confidential info is commingled
rules.atomic_rule: A request may not be denied on the ground that confidential information is commingled with the requested nonconfidential information; the agency must segregate.
rules.trigger: Requested nonconfidential info is commingled with confidential info
rules.source_language: No request to inspect, examine, or obtain copies of public records shall be denied on the grounds that confidential information is commingled with the requested nonconfidential information.
rules.notes: Segregability requirement; drives a redact-and-produce path rather than denial.

rules.legal_concept: Agency bears cost of separating confidential from nonconfidential
rules.atomic_rule: When separation of confidential from nonconfidential information is necessary to permit access, the public agency bears the cost of separation.
rules.trigger: Separation is necessary to permit inspection/copying
rules.source_language: If it is necessary to separate confidential from nonconfidential information in order to permit the inspection, examination, or copying of the public records, the public agency shall bear the cost of such separation.
rules.notes: Cost-bearer is fixed by state (agency); a city cannot shift separation cost to the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Withholding of specific business/industrial project records
rules.atomic_rule: Records relating to the proposed expansion or location of a specific business or industrial project may be withheld so long as inspection or copying would frustrate the purpose for which they were created.
rules.trigger: Record relates to proposed expansion/location of a specific business or industrial project and disclosure would frustrate its purpose
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (a) and (b) of this section, public records relating to the proposed expansion or location of specific business or industrial projects may be withheld so long as their inspection, examination or copying would frustrate the purpose for which such public records were created; provided, however, that nothing herein shall be construed to permit the withholding of public records relating to general economic development policies or activities.
rules.notes: Creates a temporary withhold state that ends on announcement/final decision; general economic development records not covered.

rules.legal_concept: 25-business-day disclosure after project announcement
rules.atomic_rule: Once the withholding basis no longer applies, the agency must disclose the requested announced-project records (not otherwise confidential) as soon as practicable and within 25 business days.
rules.trigger: Withholding basis under § 132-6(d) no longer applies (project announced/committed or final decision not to proceed)
rules.clock_spec: 25 business-days from the point the withholding basis ceases (as soon as practicable)
rules.source_language: Once the provisions of this subsection no longer apply, the agency shall disclose as soon as practicable, and within 25 business days, public records requested for the announced project that are not otherwise made confidential by law.
rules.notes: One of the few hard numeric deadlines in NC's public-records law; state-fixed at 25 business days.

rules.legal_concept: 25-business-day disclosure for qualifying-site records
rules.atomic_rule: Once the qualifying-site withholding basis no longer applies, the agency must disclose the requested qualifying-site records (not otherwise confidential) as soon as practicable and within 25 business days.
rules.trigger: Qualifying site (megasite/selectsite) acquired, or evaluated and deemed unsuitable, so § 132-6(d1) withholding ceases
rules.clock_spec: 25 business-days from the point the withholding basis ceases (as soon as practicable)
rules.source_language: Once the provisions of this subsection no longer apply, the agency shall disclose as soon as practicable, and within 25 business days, public records requested for the qualifying site that are not otherwise made confidential by law.
rules.notes: Parallel to § 132-6(d) but for state-funded megasite/selectsite acquisition. Same 25-business-day parameter, different trigger.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable restrictions to preserve fragile records
rules.atomic_rule: Inspection or copying of a record that could be damaged due to its age or condition may be made subject to reasonable restrictions intended to preserve the record.
rules.trigger: Record could be damaged during inspection/copying because of its age or condition
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (a) and (a1) of this section, the inspection or copying of any public record which, because of its age or condition could be damaged during inspection or copying, may be made subject to reasonable restrictions intended to preserve the particular record.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable restrictions' is a soft standard; the city sets the specific handling restrictions under it.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may elect media/format of copies
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may elect to obtain copies in any and all media in which the agency is capable of providing them.
rules.trigger: Requester requests copies in a particular medium
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of public records may elect to obtain them in any and all media in which the public agency is capable of providing them.
rules.notes: Requester-driven format branch, bounded by agency capability.

rules.legal_concept: No denial because agency prefers another medium
rules.atomic_rule: A request for copies in a particular medium may not be denied on the ground that the custodian has made or prefers another medium.
rules.trigger: Requester requests a particular medium the agency is capable of providing
rules.source_language: No request for copies of public records in a particular medium shall be denied on the grounds that the custodian has made or prefers to make the public records available in another medium.
rules.notes: Blocks a denial action; paired with the format-election permission.

rules.legal_concept: Different fees for different media as prescribed by law
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may assess different fees for different media, as prescribed by law.
rules.trigger: Copies provided in a particular medium
rules.source_language: The public agency may assess different fees for different media as prescribed by law.
rules.notes: Per-medium fee value is set 'as prescribed by law'; still bounded by the actual-cost ceiling in § 132-6.2(b).

rules.legal_concept: Fees for certifying copies as provided by law
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may request certified or uncertified copies; fees for certifying copies are as provided by law.
rules.trigger: Requester requests certified copies
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of public records may request that the copies be certified or uncertified. The fees for certifying copies of public records shall be as provided by law.
rules.notes: Certification fee value fixed by other law; the actual-cost ceiling applies only to uncertified copies.

rules.legal_concept: Uncertified-copy fee may not exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may not charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the agency of making the copy.
rules.trigger: Charging a fee for an uncertified copy
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of making the copy
rules.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, no public agency shall charge a fee for an uncertified copy of a public record that exceeds the actual cost to the public agency of making the copy.
rules.notes: Ceiling constraint; the city fills the operative rate under the actual-cost cap. Same concept as a fixed-rate state, different basis.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'actual cost'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Actual cost' is limited to direct, chargeable costs of reproduction per generally accepted accounting principles and excludes costs that would have been incurred anyway had no request been made.
rules.trigger: Computing an uncertified-copy fee
rules.source_language: For purposes of this subsection, "actual cost" is limited to direct, chargeable costs related to the reproduction of a public record as determined by generally accepted accounting principles and does not include costs that would have been incurred by the public agency if a request to reproduce a public record had not been made.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on to bound the fee ceiling; excludes fixed/overhead costs.

rules.legal_concept: Special service charge for extensive IT/clerical use
rules.atomic_rule: Where a request requires extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge a reasonable special service charge (based on actual cost) in addition to duplication cost.
rules.trigger: Request requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, or the requested medium causes greater IT-resource use than the agency established for that volume
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding the provisions of this subsection, if the request is such as to require extensive use of information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance by personnel of the agency involved, or if producing the record in the medium requested results in a greater use of information technology resources than that established by the agency for reproduction of the volume of information requested, then the agency may charge, in addition to the actual cost of duplication, a special service charge, which shall be reasonable and shall be based on the actual cost incurred for such extensive use of information technology resources or the labor costs of the personnel providing the services, or for a greater use of information technology resources that is actually incurred by the agency or attributable to the agency.
rules.notes: Charge must be 'reasonable' (soft) and based on actual cost; 'extensive' is an undefined trigger threshold. City sets the operative charge under the reasonableness standard.

rules.legal_concept: Fee-dispute mediation by State Chief Information Officer
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who believes a charged fee is unfair or unreasonable may ask the State Chief Information Officer (or designee) to mediate the fee dispute.
rules.trigger: Requester charged a fee it believes unfair or unreasonable
rules.source_language: If anyone requesting public information from any public agency is charged a fee that the requester believes to be unfair or unreasonable, the requester may ask the State Chief Information Officer or his designee to mediate the dispute.
rules.notes: A distinct NC review/mediation path for fee disputes, separate from judicial enforcement.

rules.legal_concept: Computer-database copy requests may be required in writing
rules.atomic_rule: For copies of computer databases, the agency may require the request to be made or submitted in writing.
rules.trigger: Request is for copies of a computer database
rules.source_language: Persons requesting copies of computer databases may be required to make or submit such requests in writing.
rules.notes: Writing may be required only for computer-database copies; no general written-request mandate for ordinary records (see material negative).

rules.legal_concept: Prompt response to computer-database requests
rules.atomic_rule: Custodians must respond to computer-database copy requests as promptly as possible, and if granted provide copies as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Computer-database copy request received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" to respond / "as soon as reasonably possible" to provide, from request receipt
rules.source_language: Custodians of public records shall respond to all such requests as promptly as possible. If the request is granted, the copies shall be provided as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft deadlines; Config Home structural. Applies specifically to computer-database requests.

rules.legal_concept: Database denial must include basis explanation
rules.atomic_rule: If a computer-database copy request is denied, the denial must be accompanied by an explanation of the basis for the denial.
rules.trigger: Computer-database copy request is denied
rules.source_language: If the request is denied, the denial shall be accompanied by an explanation of the basis for the denial.
rules.notes: Statutory duty to give a reason applies to computer-database denials; no general statutory written-denial mandate for all record types.

rules.legal_concept: Reduce database-denial explanation to writing on request
rules.atomic_rule: On request, the person denying a computer-database copy request must, as promptly as possible, reduce the explanation for the denial to writing.
rules.trigger: Requester asks that the denial explanation be put in writing
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible" from the requester's ask
rules.source_language: If asked to do so, the person denying the request shall, as promptly as possible, reduce the explanation for the denial to writing.
rules.notes: Written explanation is triggered by the requester's ask; soft timing standard.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to respond outside usual business hours
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to respond to copy requests outside of its usual business hours.
rules.trigger: Request would require response outside usual business hours
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to respond to requests for copies of public records outside of its usual business hours.
rules.notes: Bounds when the promptness clock runs (business hours only).

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create or compile a nonexistent record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to respond by creating or compiling a record that does not exist.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating/compiling a nonexistent record
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to respond to a request for a copy of a public record by creating or compiling a record that does not exist.
rules.notes: Classification gate: no-such-record path.

rules.legal_concept: Negotiated charge for voluntarily created records
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency voluntarily elects, as a service, to create or compile a record, it may negotiate a reasonable charge for the service with the requester.
rules.trigger: Agency voluntarily elects to create/compile a record as a service
rules.source_language: If a public agency, as a service to the requester, voluntarily elects to create or compile a record, it may negotiate a reasonable charge for the service with the requester.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable' negotiated charge; a soft-standard fee value the parties set.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to put a non-electronic record into electronic medium
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to put into electronic medium a record that is not kept in electronic medium.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic format for a record not kept in electronic medium
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a public agency to put into electronic medium a record that is not kept in electronic medium.
rules.notes: Bounds the format-election right: election limited to media the agency is capable of and already keeps.

rules.legal_concept: Online database access satisfies § 132-6 duty
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy the § 132-6 database-access duty by making database records individually available online (viewable/printable/savable), but must still allow inspection of any such records it also maintains in a nondigital medium.
rules.trigger: Agency provides individual online access to computer-database records
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding G.S. 132-6.2(a), a public agency may satisfy the requirement under G.S. 132-6 to provide access to public records in computer databases by making public records in computer databases individually available online in a format that allows a person to view the public record and print or save the public record to obtain a copy. A public agency that provides access to public records under this subsection is not required to provide access to the public records in the computer database in any other way; provided, however, that a public agency that provides access to public records in computer databases shall also allow inspection of any of such public records that the public agency also maintains in a nondigital medium.
rules.notes: Database-specific online-satisfaction branch with a nondigital-inspection carve-out.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a computer database not otherwise created
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to create a computer database it has not otherwise created or is not otherwise required to create.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a new computer database
rules.source_language: Nothing in this section shall require a public agency to create a computer database that the public agency has not otherwise created or is not otherwise required to be created.
rules.notes: Database analogue of the no-duty-to-create rule.

rules.legal_concept: Superior Court action to compel disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access to or copies of public records may apply to the appropriate division of the General Court of Justice for an order compelling disclosure or copying; such actions are set for immediate hearing and given priority.
rules.trigger: Person denied access or copies of public records
rules.source_language: Any person who is denied access to public records for purposes of inspection and examination, or who is denied copies of public records, may apply to the appropriate division of the General Court of Justice for an order compelling disclosure or copying, and the court shall have jurisdiction to issue such orders if the person has complied with G.S. 7A-38.3E. Actions brought pursuant to this section shall be set down for immediate hearing, and subsequent proceedings in such actions shall be accorded priority by the trial and appellate courts.
rules.notes: NC's enforcement path is judicial (mandamus-type), not administrative. Immediate-hearing/priority is a procedural directive to the court, not a request-handling clock.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory mediation before court may compel disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: The court has jurisdiction to compel disclosure only if the person has complied with G.S. 7A-38.3E (mediation of public-records disputes).
rules.trigger: Person seeks a court order compelling disclosure under § 132-9
rules.source_language: ...and the court shall have jurisdiction to issue such orders if the person has complied with G.S. 7A-38.3E.
rules.notes: Pre-suit mediation is a jurisdictional prerequisite. The terms/timeline of G.S. 7A-38.3E were not opened this pass and require verification in a later pass.

material_negatives.note: NC sets no fixed numeric acknowledgment or response deadline for ordinary public-records requests. The only timing standard is the soft 'as promptly as possible' in § 132-6(a) (captured as rule NC-0005). Absence of a found numeric rule is not proof none exists.
No statutory clarification-and-narrowing clock or deemed-abandonment-for-nonresponse provision found in Chapter 132. NC statute does not create a clarification round-trip with a deadline.

No statutory deemed/constructive-denial trigger (e.g., 'silence for N days = denial') found in Chapter 132. Enforcement under § 132-9 is available upon a denial of access/copies but the statute does not define a silence-based constructive denial.

No administrative or Attorney-General appeal stage exists for public-records denials; the remedy is a Superior Court action under § 132-9 (after G.S. 7A-38.3E mediation). A fee-specific mediation path via the State CIO exists separately (NC-0022).

No statutory requirement that ordinary (non-computer-database) public-records requests be submitted in writing; writing may be required only for computer-database copies (§ 132-6.2(c), captured as NC-0023).

No general statutory deposit/prepayment or cost-estimate-before-work rule found in Chapter 132. § 132-6(a) conditions furnishing copies on 'payment of any fees as may be prescribed by law' but sets no deposit mechanism.
No explicit search or record-identification time standard beyond the general 'as promptly as possible' promptness requirement.

Chapter 132 defines 'custodian' and excludes agencies that merely store/safekeep or provide data processing for others (§ 132-6(a)), but states no explicit wrong-department routing/forwarding duty for a misdirected request.

structural_branches.description: Online-availability path (§ 132-6(a1)): if the agency maintains a record online in viewable/printable/savable form, the copy-production obligation can be satisfied without providing copies any other way.
Database-specific online-satisfaction path (§ 132-6.1(a1)) with a mandatory carve-out that nondigital-medium copies of the same records must still be open to inspection.

Economic-development withhold-then-disclose fork (§ 132-6(d)): specific business/industrial project records enter a temporary withhold state that terminates on announcement/final decision, triggering a 25-business-day disclosure clock (NC-0012).
Qualifying-site (megasite/selectsite) parallel fork (§ 132-6(d1)) with its own withhold state and 25-business-day disclosure clock (NC-0013).
Fee-dispute mediation path through the State Chief Information Officer (§ 132-6.2(b)) — a non-judicial review stage unique to fee unfairness/unreasonableness claims.
Mandatory pre-suit mediation under G.S. 7A-38.3E as a jurisdictional gate before a § 132-9 court action to compel disclosure can proceed.
Judicial enforcement stage (§ 132-9): Superior Court action to compel disclosure/copying, set for immediate hearing and given priority — NC has no administrative appeal alternative.

rules.legal_concept: Right of inspection limited to Tennessee citizens
rules.atomic_rule: Access under the TPRA runs to any citizen of Tennessee; those in charge of records shall not refuse inspection to any citizen unless otherwise provided by state law.
rules.trigger: Any request for personal inspection of a state, county, or municipal record.
rules.source_language: All state, county and municipal records shall, at all times during business hours, which for public hospitals shall be during the business hours of their administrative offices, be open for personal inspection by any citizen of this state, and those in charge of the records shall not refuse such right of inspection to any citizen, unless otherwise provided by state law.
rules.effective_status: Current (verified against 2021 codification; core provisions unchanged in 2024 code)
rules.notes: Tennessee is a citizen-restricted state; does NOT satisfy eligibility.any_person or eligibility.no_residency_requirement. Tennessee Supreme Court has construed 'citizen' to include incarcerated Tennessee inmates. Entity may elect to serve non-citizens (see TN-0003).

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose / intended use required
rules.atomic_rule: The TPRA does not distinguish requests based on the requester's intended use; a requester need not state a purpose to access open records.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional).
rules.source_language: The TPRA does not distinguish requests for inspection of records based on intended use, be it for research, personal, or commercial purposes. Likewise, this Schedule of Reasonable Charges does not make a distinction in the charges assessed based on the purpose of a record request.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F (implementing Tenn. Code Ann. § 8-4-604); Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key per instructions. Narrow exception: certain documents requested for a specific commercial use carry special fees under § 10-7-506(c) (see TN-0040).

rules.legal_concept: Entity may choose to serve non-Tennessee-citizens
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may determine, in its public records policy, whether to respond to TPRA requests from persons who are not citizens of Tennessee.
rules.trigger: Adoption of the entity's public records policy.
