rules.source_language: The TPRA authorizes a governmental entity to determine the following with respect to each entity's public records policy: A. Whether to respond to TPRA requests by persons who are not citizens of Tennessee;
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy, Policy Considerations § I.A
rules.notes: City-elected branch: a locally-filled fork on whether the citizenship gate (TN-0001) is enforced.

rules.legal_concept: Optional government-issued photo ID as prerequisite to access
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may require government-issued photo identification as a prerequisite to providing access to records.
rules.trigger: Adoption of the entity's public records policy electing to require ID.
rules.source_language: The TPRA authorizes a governmental entity to determine the following with respect to each entity's public records policy: ... B. Whether to require government-issued photo identification as a prerequisite to providing access to records;
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy, Policy Considerations § I.B; statutory basis Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(vi)
rules.notes: OORC FAQ states the photo ID 'includes an address.' Exact verbatim of statutory subsection (a)(7)(A)(vi) not opened; the permission itself is verbatim from the OORC Model Policy. City-elected branch.

rules.legal_concept: No written request or charge to view a record
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity shall not require a written request or assess a charge merely to view (inspect) a public record, unless otherwise required by law.
rules.trigger: A request to view (inspect only) a public record.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall not require a written request or assess a charge to view a public record unless otherwise required by law.
rules.notes: Distinguish inspection (no writing, no fee) from copies (writing/form and fees permitted — TN-0007, TN-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Permitted channels for submitting inspection requests
rules.atomic_rule: Requests to view public records may be submitted in person, by telephone, fax, mail, or email (if the entity uses such means for official business), or via internet portal (if the entity maintains one for records requests).
rules.trigger: A request to view public records.
rules.source_language: Requests to view public records may be submitted in person or by telephone, fax, mail, or email if the governmental entity uses such means of communication to transact official business, or via internet portal if the governmental entity maintains an internet portal that is used for accepting public records requests.

rules.legal_concept: Entity may require copy requests in writing or on a form
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may require a request for COPIES of public records to be in writing, on a form complying with subsection (c), or on a form developed by the Office of Open Records Counsel.
rules.trigger: A request for copies (as opposed to inspection only).
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may require a request for copies of public records to be: In writing; On a form that complies with subsection (c); or On a form developed by the office of open records counsel.
rules.notes: City-elected branch. If a form is required for copies it must be attached to the entity's public records policy.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be sufficiently detailed
rules.atomic_rule: Any request for inspection or copying must be sufficiently detailed to enable the governmental entity to identify the specific records sought.
rules.trigger: Submission of a records request.
rules.source_language: Any request for inspection or copying of a public record shall be sufficiently detailed to enable the governmental entity to identify the specific records for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Gate for lack-of-specificity denial (TN-0027) and clarification assistance (TN-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Offer to assist narrowing/clarifying a non-specific request
rules.atomic_rule: If a request lacks specificity, the coordinator/custodian may deny for lack of specificity while offering to assist in clarification, or contact the requestor to see if the request can be narrowed.
rules.trigger: A request that is not sufficiently detailed, or is for a large volume of records.
rules.source_language: The request lacks specificity. (Offer to assist in clarification) ... If appropriate, contact the requestor to see if the request can be narrowed.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy §§ III.A.2.b.ii, III.A.2.c
rules.notes: No statutory clarification clock: the TPRA does not toll or restart the 7-business-day clock while clarification is sought (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: No duty to compile, create, or recreate records
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity is not required to sort through files to compile information or to create or recreate a record that does not exist.
rules.trigger: A request that would require compiling information or creating a nonexistent record.
rules.source_language: This section shall not be construed as requiring a governmental entity to sort through files to compile information or to create or recreate a record that does not exist.
rules.notes: Supports 'no such record exists' denial ground (TN-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Public Records Request Coordinator (PRRC) routing duty
rules.atomic_rule: The Public Records Request Coordinator ensures that public records requests are routed to the appropriate records custodian and that requests are fulfilled in accordance with § 10-7-503(a)(2)(B).
rules.trigger: Receipt of a public records request by the entity.
rules.source_language: "Public records request coordinator" means any individual within a governmental entity whose role it is to ensure that public records requests are routed to the appropriate records custodian and that requests are fulfilled in accordance with § 10-7-503(a)(2)(B).
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #1 (custodian designation / routing). Secondary type: Requirement. Every county/municipal policy must name the PRRC (see TN-0046).

rules.legal_concept: Referral when another entity is the custodian
rules.atomic_rule: If requested records are in the custody of a different governmental entity and the correct entity is known, the coordinator advises the requestor of the correct entity and its coordinator.
rules.trigger: Requested records are held by a different governmental entity than the one receiving the request.
rules.source_language: If requested records are in the custody of a different governmental entity, and the PRRC knows the correct governmental entity, the PRRC should advise the requestor of the correct governmental entity and PRRC for that entity if known.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.A.2.e
rules.notes: Also a permitted denial ground where the entity is not the custodian (TN-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Cannot avoid disclosure by delegating to a private entity
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity is prohibited from avoiding its disclosure obligations by contractually delegating its responsibility to a private entity.
rules.trigger: Records held by a private entity under contract with the governmental entity.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity is prohibited from avoiding its disclosure obligations by contractually delegating its responsibility to a private entity.
rules.notes: Blocks a 'private contractor holds it' denial; affects coverage/routing of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt availability for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian or the custodian's designee shall promptly make available for inspection any public record not specifically exempt from disclosure.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a request to inspect a non-exempt public record.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from request receipt
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record or the custodian's designee shall promptly make available for inspection any public record not specifically exempt from disclosure.
rules.notes: 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard — do not convert to a day count. The 7-business-day rule (TN-0015) applies only when prompt availability is not practicable.

rules.legal_concept: Seven-business-day response requirement
rules.atomic_rule: When it is not practicable for a record to be promptly available, the custodian shall within seven (7) business days take one of three actions: (i) make it available, (ii) deny in writing with basis, or (iii) furnish in writing the time reasonably necessary to produce it.
rules.trigger: It is not practicable for the record to be promptly available for inspection.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 7 business-days from custodian's receipt of the request
rules.source_language: In the event it is not practicable for the record to be promptly available for inspection, the custodian shall, within seven (7) business days: Make the information available to the requestor; Deny the request in writing or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel. The response shall include the basis for the denial; or Furnish the requester in writing, or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.notes: Fixed statutory window (business days, not calendar). This is the core response clock; branches into three outcomes (TN-0016, TN-0026) and, on silence, deemed denial (TN-0017).

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of time reasonably necessary to produce
rules.atomic_rule: As the third permitted response, the custodian furnishes the requester, in writing or on the OORC response form, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.trigger: Custodian elects option (iii) within the 7-business-day window because more time is needed.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "time reasonably necessary to produce" stated by custodian, from request receipt
rules.source_language: Furnish the requester in writing, or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel, the time reasonably necessary to produce the record or information.
rules.notes: The production deadline is a custodian-stated soft standard, not a fixed statutory number.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive (deemed) denial on failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond as described in subdivision (a)(2) constitutes a denial, and the requester has the right to bring an action under § 10-7-505.
rules.trigger: Custodian fails to take any of the (a)(2)(B) actions within seven business days.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: silence past 7 business-days = denial, triggering § 10-7-505 action
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to the request as described in subdivision (a)(2) shall constitute a denial and the person making the request shall have the right to bring an action as provided in § 10-7-505.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3 (deemed/constructive denial trigger). Terminal event; leads to judicial petition (TN-0042).

rules.legal_concept: No charge for inspection of open records
rules.atomic_rule: Records custodians may not charge for inspection of public records except as provided by law.
rules.trigger: A request to inspect (view) open public records.
rules.source_language: Records custodians may not charge for inspection of public records except as provided by law.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.A; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(A)(i)
rules.notes: Fixed at $0 for inspection. Copy and labor charges are separate (TN-0029 et seq.).

rules.legal_concept: Most economical and efficient production
rules.atomic_rule: When assessing fees for copies, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.
rules.trigger: A request for copies of public records.
rules.source_language: When assessing a fee for items covered under this section, records custodians shall utilize the most economical and efficient method of producing the requested records.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.A

rules.legal_concept: Segmented production of large-volume requests
rules.atomic_rule: If production should be segmented because of a large volume of records, the custodian uses the response form to notify the requestor that production will be in segments and a production schedule will be provided as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.trigger: Records request is for a large volume of records, or additional time is needed to prepare records for access.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: production schedule "as expeditiously as practicable" from response form notice
rules.source_language: If a records custodian reasonably determines production of records should be segmented because the records request is for a large volume of records, or additional time is necessary to prepare the records for access, the records custodian shall use the Public Records Request Response Form to notify the requestor that production of the records will be in segments and that a records production schedule will be provided as expeditiously as practicable.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.B.4
rules.notes: Tennessee-specific production path (rolling/segmented production with a schedule).

rules.legal_concept: Cure for omitted responsive records
rules.atomic_rule: If the custodian discovers responsive records were omitted, the custodian should contact the requestor about the omission and produce the records as quickly as practicable.
rules.trigger: Discovery, after responding, that responsive records were omitted.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: produce omitted records "as quickly as practicable" from discovery
rules.source_language: If a records custodian discovers records responsive to a records request were omitted, the records custodian should contact the requestor concerning the omission and produce the records as quickly as practicable.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.B.5

rules.legal_concept: Delivery of copies when not retrieved in person
rules.atomic_rule: If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve copies and the actual delivery cost plus other permitted charges are paid or waived, the custodian must deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail; other means (including electronic) are discretionary and may carry delivery costs.
rules.trigger: Requestor elects not to retrieve copies in person.
rules.source_language: If a requestor chooses not to personally retrieve records and the actual cost of delivering the copies, in addition to any other permitted charges, have been paid by the requestor or otherwise waived pursuant to the public records policy, then a records custodian is obligated to deliver the copies via USPS First-Class Mail. It is within the discretion of a records custodian to agree to deliver copies of records through other means, including electronically, and to assess the costs related to such delivery.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § III.D

rules.legal_concept: Redaction of confidential information and release of remainder
rules.atomic_rule: Information made confidential by state law shall be redacted whenever possible, and the redacted record shall be made available for inspection and copying.
rules.trigger: A responsive record contains information made confidential by state law.
rules.source_language: Information made confidential by state law shall be redacted whenever possible, and the redacted record shall be made available for inspection and copying.
rules.notes: Segregability duty — confidential portions redacted rather than whole-record withholding.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction is not creation of a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The redaction of confidential information shall not constitute the creation of a new record.
rules.trigger: Redaction performed to release an otherwise-confidential-laden record.
rules.source_language: The redaction of confidential information shall not constitute the creation of a new record.
rules.notes: Forecloses a 'no duty to create' defense (TN-0010) as applied to redaction.

rules.legal_concept: Provide general basis for redaction
rules.atomic_rule: Whenever a redacted record is provided, the custodian should provide the requestor the basis for redaction, stated generally so as not to disclose the confidential information.
rules.trigger: A redacted record is provided to the requestor.
rules.source_language: Whenever a redacted record is provided, a records custodian should provide the requestor with the basis for redaction. The basis given for redaction shall be general in nature and not disclose confidential information.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.C.2

rules.legal_concept: Written denial stating basis (on OORC response form)
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must be in writing (or on the OORC-developed records request response form) and shall include the basis for the denial.
rules.trigger: Custodian elects to deny the request (option (ii)).
rules.source_language: Deny the request in writing or by completing a records request response form developed by the office of open records counsel. The response shall include the basis for the denial.
rules.notes: Standardized denial instrument is the OORC Public Record Request Response Form.

rules.legal_concept: Denial where state/federal law prohibits disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied where an exemption makes the record not subject to disclosure under the TPRA; the applicable exemption must be provided in the written denial.
rules.trigger: A state, federal, or other law prohibits disclosure of the requested record.
rules.source_language: An exemption makes the record not subject to disclosure under the TPRA. (Provide the exemption in written denial)
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy § III.A.2.b.iii
rules.notes: Exemptions themselves (§ 10-7-504 et al.) are not inventoried here; see Special Record Types.

rules.legal_concept: Denial where entity is not custodian or record does not exist
rules.atomic_rule: A request may be denied where the governmental entity is not the custodian of the requested records, or the records do not exist.
rules.trigger: Entity does not hold the records, or no responsive record exists.
rules.source_language: The Governmental Entity is not the custodian of the requested records. ... The records do not exist.
rules.source_authority: OORC Model Public Records Policy §§ III.A.2.b.iv, III.A.2.b.v
rules.notes: Pairs with no-duty-to-create (TN-0010) and wrong-entity referral (TN-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Per-page charge for black-and-white copies
rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 black-and-white copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15).
rules.trigger: Production of standard-size black-and-white copies.
rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of up to 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies ... If producing duplex (front and back) copies, a charge for two separate pages may be imposed for each single duplex copy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
rules.notes: Ceiling (up to $0.15). City sets the operative rate at or below this in its policy; a higher rate requires documented actual-cost analysis (TN-0031). Duplex counts as two pages.

rules.legal_concept: Per-page charge for color copies
rules.atomic_rule: For each standard 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 color copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per-page charge of up to 50 cents ($0.50).
rules.trigger: Production of standard-size color copies.
rules.source_language: For each standard 8 1/2" x 11" or 8 1/2" x 14" copy produced, a records custodian may assess a per page charge of ... up to 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.A
rules.notes: Ceiling. If color is dearer and the record can be produced in B&W, the custodian must advise the requestor it can be produced in B&W unless the requestor will pay the higher color charge (Schedule § II.B).

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost charges above the schedule with documentation
rules.atomic_rule: If actual costs are higher than the schedule amounts, or records are produced on a non-standard medium, the entity may develop its own charges but must document 'actual cost' calculation and reasoning in an adopted policy; charges above $0.15 (B&W) / $0.50 (color) require documented actual-cost analysis.
rules.trigger: Actual production cost exceeds the schedule amounts, or non-standard medium is used.
rules.source_language: If a governmental entity's actual costs are higher than those reflected above ... the governmental entity may develop its own charges. The governmental entity must establish a schedule of charges documenting "actual cost" and state the calculation and reasoning for its charges in a properly adopted policy. ... Charges greater than 15 cents ($0.15) for black and white copies and 50 cents ($0.50) for color copies can be assessed or collected only when there is documented analysis of the fact that the higher charges represent the governmental entity's actual cost of producing such material, unless there exists another basis in law for such charges.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § II.C
rules.notes: Same concept as the ceiling rows (TN-0029/0030) under a different basis — do not split as a separate rate; this is the escape valve above the guideline ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: First hour of labor not chargeable (labor threshold)
rules.atomic_rule: The labor threshold is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material; a governmental entity may adopt a higher threshold, and labor may be charged only for time exceeding the threshold.
rules.trigger: A request for copies requiring labor to locate, retrieve, review, redact, and reproduce records.
rules.source_language: "Labor threshold" is the first (1st) hour of labor reasonably necessary to produce requested material(s). A governmental entity may adopt a higher labor threshold than one (1) hour. A records custodian is only permitted to charge for labor exceeding the labor threshold established by the governmental entity.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § IV.C
rules.notes: Floor: minimum one free hour; city may set a higher (more generous) threshold. Aggregation removes this waiver (TN-0038).

rules.legal_concept: Labor rate = hourly wage of employee(s) reasonably necessary
rules.atomic_rule: Labor above the threshold is charged at the hourly wage of the employee(s) reasonably necessary, using the lowest practicable wage; the hourly wage is the employee's base salary (excluding benefits), computed by dividing annual salary by required hours per year.
rules.trigger: Labor time exceeds the labor threshold.
rules.source_language: "Labor" is the time (in hours) reasonably necessary to produce requested records, including the time spent locating, retrieving, reviewing, redacting, and reproducing records. ... "Hourly wage of an employee" is based upon the base salary of the employee and does not include benefits. If an employee is not paid on an hourly basis, the hourly wage shall be determined by dividing the employee's annual salary by the required hours to be worked per year. ... In calculating labor charges, a records custodian should determine the total amount of labor for each employee and subtract the labor threshold from the labor of the highest paid employee(s).
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ IV.B, IV.D, IV.E
rules.notes: Rate is a computed value keyed to specific employees' wages, not a fixed number; the one free hour is deducted from the highest-paid employee's time.

rules.legal_concept: Itemized cost estimate before producing copies
rules.atomic_rule: The records custodian shall provide the requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material before producing them.
rules.trigger: A request for copies that will incur charges.
rules.source_language: The records custodian shall provide a requestor an estimate of the reasonable costs to provide copies of the requested material.
rules.source_authority: Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B); OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.G; OORC Model Public Records Policy § VI.B
rules.notes: Model Policy § VI.B: 'Records custodians shall provide requestors with an itemized estimate of the charges ... prior to producing copies ... and may require pre-payment.'

rules.legal_concept: Payment for copies may be required before production
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing the copies of the records.
rules.trigger: Charges are assessed for copies.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may require payment for copies before producing copies of the records.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.E; Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-503(a)(7)(B)
rules.notes: Non-payment of estimated fees is itself a permitted denial/hold ground (OORC Response Form). City sets the dollar threshold above which prepayment is required.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary reduction or waiver of charges
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
rules.trigger: Application of the entity's fee-waiver provisions.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may reduce or waive charges, in whole or in part, in accordance with the governmental entity's public records policy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.D
rules.notes: City sets waiver thresholds; fees on aggregated requests are typically non-waivable (TN-0038).

rules.legal_concept: Actual cost of storage media, outside vendor, and retrieval
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may charge actual out-of-pocket cost for flash drives/storage devices provided; if internal production is not practicable, may use an outside vendor and charge those actual costs; and may recover actual retrieval charges assessed by an archive or other entity holding the records.
rules.trigger: Electronic media supplied, outside-vendor production, or retrieval from an archive/other holder.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may charge its actual out-of-pocket costs for flash drives or similar storage devices on which electronic copies are provided. ... If it is not practicable or feasible for the records custodian to produce copies internally, the records custodian may use an outside vendor and charge the costs to the requester. ... If a records custodian is assessed a charge to retrieve requested records from archives or any other entity having possession of requested records, the records custodian may recover from the requestor the costs assessed for retrieval.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges §§ III.B, III.E, III.F
rules.notes: Actual-cost pass-throughs (basis 'fixed' = the actual amount incurred). Per-page charges for electronic records only when paper had to be produced (e.g., printed to redact).

rules.legal_concept: Aggregation threshold for frequent/multiple requests
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity's policy shall specify the number of requests within a calendar month that triggers aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests.
rules.trigger: Multiple/frequent requests within a calendar month reaching the entity's threshold.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity's public record policy shall indicate the number of requests within a calendar month that will trigger aggregation; that amount must be no lower than four (4) requests. This amount is the aggregation threshold.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.D
rules.notes: Floor: statewide minimum threshold is 4/month; the city fills the operative number at or above 4. Once reached, the labor-threshold waiver no longer applies (TN-0039).

rules.legal_concept: Loss of labor-threshold waiver once aggregation threshold met
rules.atomic_rule: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
rules.trigger: Aggregation threshold reached.
rules.source_language: Once a records custodian reaches the aggregation threshold, the records custodian is no longer required to deduct the labor threshold set forth in the Schedule of Reasonable Charges or any other minimum charge per request that would ordinarily be waived.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § II.A

rules.legal_concept: Aggregation across requestors acting in concert
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may aggregate multiple requests by a single requestor, and may aggregate requests by multiple requestors if the coordinator determines they are acting in concert with each other or as agents of another person, entity, or organization.
rules.trigger: Multiple requests by one requestor, or by several requestors the coordinator finds are acting in concert/as agents.
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may aggregate multiple public record requests made by a single requestor. A governmental entity may also aggregate public record requests made by multiple requestors, if the public records request coordinator determines the requestors are acting in concert with each other or as the agents of another person, entity, or organization.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests § I.C
rules.notes: 'Working in concert' is a coordinator determination; it is appealable to the OORC (TN-0041).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of aggregation and right to appeal to OORC
rules.atomic_rule: When aggregating, the custodian must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right to appeal that decision to the Office of Open Records Counsel; disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
rules.trigger: Custodian decides to aggregate requests upon meeting the threshold.
rules.source_language: When the aggregation threshold is met, a records custodian choosing to aggregate requests must inform the requestor(s) of the determination to aggregate and of the right of the requestor(s) to appeal the records custodian's decision to aggregate to the OORC. ... Disputes regarding aggregation shall be brought to the OORC.
rules.source_authority: OORC Reasonable Charges for Frequent and Multiple Requests §§ II.B, II.D
rules.notes: Administrative review path (OORC). OORC guidance/mediation is advisory, not a binding adjudication; the binding remedy remains the § 10-7-505 judicial petition (TN-0042). Routinely released/readily accessible records (agendas, minutes) are exempt from aggregation (Freq. policy § II.C).

rules.legal_concept: Petition for access and judicial review after denial
rules.atomic_rule: A Tennessee citizen whose request under § 10-7-503 has been denied in whole or in part may petition for access to the record and to obtain judicial review of the actions taken to deny access.
rules.trigger: Denial (including deemed denial) of an inspection request.
rules.source_language: Any citizen of Tennessee who shall request the right of personal inspection of any state, county or municipal record as provided in § 10-7-503, and whose request has been in whole or in part denied by the official and/or designee of the official or through any act or regulation of any official or designee of any official, shall be entitled to petition for access to any such record and to obtain judicial review of the actions taken to deny the access.
rules.notes: Judicial (not administrative) appeal path — namespaced appeal.judicial.*. Reached from deemed denial (TN-0017) or express denial (TN-0026).

rules.legal_concept: Venue for a public-records access petition
rules.atomic_rule: The petition is filed in chancery or circuit court (or other equity court) of the county where the county/municipal records are situated; for state records, in Davidson County, the county of the records' situs, or the petitioner's county of residence.
rules.trigger: Filing of a § 10-7-505 access petition.
rules.source_language: Such petition shall be filed in the chancery court or circuit court for the county in which the county or municipal records sought are situated, or in any other court of that county having equity jurisdiction. In the case of records in the custody and control of any state department, agency or instrumentality, such petition shall be filed in the chancery court or circuit court of Davidson County; or in the chancery court or circuit court for the county in which the state records are situated ...; or in the chancery court or circuit court in the county of the petitioner's residence ...
rules.notes: For municipal requests, venue is the county where the municipal records are situated.

rules.legal_concept: Expedited show-cause hearing on access petition
rules.atomic_rule: Upon filing, at the petitioner's request the court shall issue an order requiring the respondent to immediately appear and show cause why the petition should not be granted; no formal written response is required and ordinary response-filing periods do not apply, in the interest of expeditious hearings.
rules.trigger: Filing of the petition and petitioner's request for a show-cause order.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: respondent to "immediately appear and show cause" upon court order
rules.source_language: Upon filing of the petition, the court shall, upon request of the petitioning party, issue an order requiring the defendant or respondent party or parties to immediately appear and show cause, if they have any, why the petition should not be granted. A formal written response to the petition shall not be required, and the generally applicable periods of filing such response shall not apply in the interest of expeditious hearings.
rules.notes: Expedited-hearing standard; no fixed day-count in statute.

rules.legal_concept: Government's burden to justify nondisclosure
rules.atomic_rule: The burden of proof for justification of nondisclosure is on the official/designee, who must show justification by a preponderance of the evidence.
rules.trigger: Adjudication of a § 10-7-505 access petition.
rules.source_language: The burden of proof for justification of nondisclosure of records sought shall be upon the official and/or designee of the official of those records and the justification for the nondisclosure must be shown by a preponderance of the evidence.
rules.notes: Presumption of openness; government bears the burden. The willful-denial attorney-fee remedy in § 10-7-505(g) is excluded per the inclusion test (see Excluded).

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory written public records policy (county/municipal)
rules.atomic_rule: Every county and municipal governmental entity shall establish a written public records policy, adopted by its governing authority, that is not more burdensome than state law and includes the request process and any required form, the response process (including redaction), a statement of fees and billing/payment procedures, and the PRRC's name/title and contact information.
rules.trigger: Entity is a county or municipal governmental entity subject to the TPRA.
rules.source_language: No later than July 1, 2018, every county and municipal governmental entity subject to this section shall establish a written public records policy properly adopted by the appropriate governing authority. The public records policy shall not impose requirements on those requesting records that are more burdensome than state law and shall include: The process for making requests to inspect public records or receive copies of public records and a copy of any required request form; The process for responding to requests, including redaction practices; A statement of any fees charged for copies of public records and the procedures for billing and payment; and The name or title and the contact information of the individual or individuals within such governmental entity designated as the public records request coordinator.
rules.effective_status: Current (verified against 2021 codification; unchanged 2024). Original adoption deadline July 1, 2018 has passed.
rules.notes: This is the structural anchor for city-filled parameters (fee rates, labor threshold, ID election, copy-form election, aggregation threshold). Policy 'shall not impose requirements more burdensome than state law' is a binding ceiling on local restrictions.

rules.legal_concept: Notice to officer when law-enforcement personnel records inspected
rules.atomic_rule: Whenever a law-enforcement officer's personnel records are inspected, the custodian shall make a record of the inspection and, within three (3) days of the inspection, notify the officer that the inspection took place, the inspector's name/address/telephone number, for whom the inspection was made, and the date.
rules.trigger: Inspection of the personnel records of a law-enforcement officer.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 3 days from the date of inspection to notify the officer
rules.source_language: whenever the personnel records of a law enforcement officer are inspected as provided in subsection (a), the custodian shall make a record of such inspection and provide notice, within three (3) days from the date of the inspection, to the officer whose personnel records have been inspected: That such inspection has taken place; The name, address and telephone number of the person making such inspection; For whom the inspection was made; and The date of such inspection.
rules.notes: Creates a distinct post-inspection notice workflow with a fixed 3-day clock. Special-record processing rule.

rules.legal_concept: Inspector identification for law-enforcement personnel records
rules.atomic_rule: A person inspecting law-enforcement personnel records must provide their name, address, business and home telephone numbers, driver license number, or other appropriate identification prior to inspecting the records.
rules.trigger: A person seeks to inspect law-enforcement officer personnel records.
rules.source_language: Any person making an inspection of such records shall provide such person's name, address, business telephone number, home telephone number, driver license number or other appropriate identification prior to inspecting such records.
rules.notes: Feeds the notice content in TN-0047. This mandatory identification is an exception to the general no-ID-required baseline (contrasts with the optional photo-ID election, TN-0004).

rules.legal_concept: Special fees for specific documents requested for a specific use
rules.atomic_rule: Although standard copy/labor charges do not vary by purpose, other statutory provisions (e.g., § 10-7-506(c)) enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use.
rules.trigger: Request for specific enumerated documents for a specific (e.g., commercial) use governed by § 10-7-506(c).
rules.source_language: However, other statutory provisions, such as Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c), enumerate fees that may be assessed when specific documents are requested for a specific use. Any distinctions made, or waiver of charges permitted, based upon the type of records requested should be expressly set forth and permitted in the adopted public records policy.
rules.source_authority: OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges § I.F, citing Tenn. Code Ann. § 10-7-506(c)
rules.effective_status: Requires manual verification of § 10-7-506(c) enumerated documents/rates
rules.notes: The verbatim capture is the OORC Schedule's reference; the specific documents and fee amounts in § 10-7-506(c) were not opened verbatim and need a later pass. Flags human legal review.

rules.legal_concept: Statutory authority to charge reasonable production costs
rules.atomic_rule: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material, assessed in the manner established by the Office of Open Records Counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
rules.trigger: A request for copies/production of public records.
rules.source_language: A records custodian may require a requestor to pay the custodian's reasonable costs incurred in producing the requested material and to assess the reasonable costs in the manner established by the office of open records counsel pursuant to § 8-4-604.
rules.notes: Statutory hook that makes the OORC Schedule of Reasonable Charges the operative cost framework. § 10-7-506(a) separately grants custodians the right to adopt and enforce reasonable rules governing the making of copies (per OORC Model Policy, Policy Considerations).
